If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to offset pessimism.  
If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative in mid-horizon (8–15 days), reduce forecast by 2–4% in mid-horizon to reflect sentiment reversal.  
If sentiment remains neutral (0.00–0.33) across 3+ days, apply no correction in early horizon but reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% in late horizon (16–30 days) to avoid flatness bias.  
If sentiment is positive but recent price is trending down, reduce forecast by 1–2% in mid-horizon to align with momentum reversal.  
If sentiment is negative but recent price is trending up, increase forecast by 1–2% in mid-horizon to counteract sentiment-driven overcorrection.
